title: Fibonacci Playbook
html:
The levels

LevelMeaning
23.6%Shallow pullback — strong trends often only pull back this far
38.2%Healthy pullback in a strong trend
50%Not a true Fibonacci ratio, but widely watched — the "halfway" test
61.8%The "golden ratio" — the classic deep-pullback buy zone; a break below often means the trend is failing
78.6%Last line before a full retracement
127.2% / 161.8%Extensions — upside (or downside) targets beyond the prior high (or low)

How to draw

  • Uptrend: anchor at the swing low, drag to the swing high. Retracement levels below price are potential support (buy zones).
  • Downtrend: anchor at the swing high, drag to the swing low. Retracement levels above price are potential resistance (where bounces stall).
  • Use clear, obvious swings — the ones every trader can see. Fib works partly because many people watch the same levels.
  • Draw on multiple timeframes: weekly for the big picture, daily for trades.

Making it stronger: confluence

A Fib level is much more meaningful when it lines up with:

  • the 20-, 50- or 200-day moving average
  • a prior swing high/low (old resistance becomes support)
  • a Fib level from a different swing (a "Fib cluster")
  • a round number ($750, $350)

Trading rules (draft)

  • Don't buy just because price touched a level — wait for a reaction (reversal candle, close back above the level).
  • Stop goes just beyond the next Fib level.
  • First target = the prior swing high/low; second target = 127.2% extension.
  • Reward should be at least 2x the risk.

People to study

Carolyn Boroden (Fibonacci Trading), Robert Fischer (Fibonacci Applications and Strategies for Traders), Robert Prechter (Elliott Wave + Fib), Tom DeMark (DeMark indicators, exhaustion counts). See Technical Funds & Traders.
